evals.name: spawn-single-agent-mcp
evals.description: Spawn a single agent using spawn_agent MCP — the canonical method
evals.prompt: I need you to run a cursor CLI audit on the golems repo to check for unused imports. Open it in a cmux pane so I can see it working.

assertions.name: uses-spawn-agent-mcp
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__spawn_agent MCP tool with cli='cursor', repo='golems'

assertions.name: descriptive-prompt
assertions.description: Passes a clear task prompt describing the unused imports audit

assertions.name: no-manual-cmux-send
assertions.description: Does NOT manually use cmux send_input + cd + cursor commands to hand-roll the launch

assertions.name: no-hand-rolled-shell-chain
assertions.description: Does NOT write 'cd ~/Gits/golems && cursor ...' via send_input

evals.name: parallel-spawn-wait-read-pipeline
evals.description: Full spawn→wait→read pipeline: spawn 2 agents, wait for both, read structured output
evals.prompt: Spawn 2 Claude workers: one in brainlayer to fix search ranking, one in golems to add retry wrapper. Wait until both finish, then summarize their results.

assertions.name: spawns-both-via-mcp
assertions.description: Calls mcp__cmuxlayer__spawn_agent twice — once for brainlayer, once for golems

assertions.name: targets-correct-repos
assertions.description: First spawn targets repo='brainlayer', second targets repo='golems'

assertions.name: waits-for-all
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__wait_for_all with both agent IDs and target_state='done'

assertions.name: reads-structured-output
assertions.description: After wait completes, uses mcp__cmuxlayer__read_agent_output to extract results (not raw read_screen)

assertions.name: no-cron-polling
assertions.description: Does NOT use CronCreate/loop to poll — wait_for_all blocks natively

assertions.name: no-sleep-polling
assertions.description: Does NOT use sleep loops or manual polling to check completion

evals.name: codex-agent-routing
evals.description: Codex agents use correct cli parameter and model via spawn_agent
evals.prompt: Run a Codex agent on the golems repo to refactor the retry wrapper. Full auto, no prompts.

assertions.name: uses-spawn-agent-mcp
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__spawn_agent with cli='codex'

assertions.name: includes-handoff-request
assertions.description: Prompt includes handoff summary request (files modified, decisions, TODOs)

assertions.name: no-old-codex-exec-syntax
assertions.description: Does NOT use old 'codex exec -m -s' syntax via send_input

evals.name: workers-splits-audits-workspaces
evals.description: Rule 5: Workers stay visible as current-workspace splits; audits/research use separate named workspaces unless explicitly requested otherwise.
evals.prompt: I need two agents: a Claude worker to implement a caching layer in golems (coding work), and a Cursor audit to review error handling across brainlayer (read-only audit). Set them up in cmux.

assertions.name: spawns-both-agents
assertions.description: Uses spawn_agent for both the worker and the audit

assertions.name: worker-is-current-workspace-split
assertions.description: The coding worker is placed in a visible split in the current workspace

assertions.name: audit-is-separate-named-workspace
assertions.description: The read-only audit/research agent is placed in a separate named workspace such as 'Audit: brainlayer'

assertions.name: distinguishes-task-types
assertions.description: Treats the worker (implementation) differently from the audit (read-only) in terms of layout

evals.name: sequential-launch-biometric-delay
evals.description: Rule 6: 3s between spawns for biometric (Touch ID) authentication
evals.prompt: Spawn 3 Claude workers: one in golems for search-fix, one in brainlayer for KG-rebuild, one in voicelayer for TTS-latency. All Sonnet, all need to run in parallel.

assertions.name: spawns-all-three
assertions.description: Uses spawn_agent three times for all three repos

assertions.name: sequential-not-simultaneous
assertions.description: Spawns agents sequentially (not all at once) — mentions waiting, staggering, or 3-second delay between spawns

assertions.name: mentions-biometric-or-touchid
assertions.description: Acknowledges the 3s delay is for biometric/Touch ID or system prompt authentication

assertions.name: no-simultaneous-spawn
assertions.description: Does NOT fire all 3 spawn_agent calls in a single parallel batch

evals.name: list-surfaces-before-send
evals.description: Rule 2: Discover surfaces via list_surfaces or list_agents BEFORE sending to any surface
evals.prompt: Send a message to the agent working on brainlayer search fix — tell it to also check the entity resolution pipeline.

assertions.name: discovers-first
assertions.description: Calls list_surfaces or list_agents BEFORE send_input or send_to_agent

assertions.name: sends-message
assertions.description: Uses send_to_agent (if agent_id known) or send_input (if only surface known)

assertions.name: no-blind-send
assertions.description: Does NOT send to a hardcoded or guessed surface ID without discovering first

evals.name: send-input-send-key-paired
evals.description: send_input must ALWAYS be followed by send_key Return to execute the command
evals.prompt: Run 'bun test' on surface:301 to check if the tests pass.

assertions.name: calls-send-input
assertions.description: Uses send_input to type 'bun test' on surface:301

assertions.name: calls-send-key-return
assertions.description: Follows send_input with send_key(key='Return') to execute the command

assertions.name: correct-order
assertions.description: send_input comes BEFORE send_key — not reversed

evals.name: send-to-agent-over-send-input
evals.description: Prefer send_to_agent (by agent ID) over send_input (by surface) when agent ID is known
evals.prompt: Send this info to agent:xyz which is working on the security audit: 'JWT refresh tokens are not being rotated on use — this is a token reuse vulnerability.'

assertions.name: uses-send-to-agent
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__send_to_agent with agent_id='agent:xyz'

assertions.name: includes-context
assertions.description: Contextualizes WHY this matters to the agent's specific security audit task

assertions.name: no-surface-send-when-id-known
assertions.description: Does NOT use send_input by surface ref when agent_id is already known

evals.name: gems-broadcast-all-agents
evals.description: Rule 15: New context MUST be broadcast to ALL active agents, contextualized per task
evals.prompt: I just found a great article about retry patterns with exponential backoff and jitter. Key insight: 'Always add jitter to prevent thundering herd — random(0, base_delay * 2^attempt)'. I have 3 agents running: agent:301 building retry wrapper in golems, agent:302 auditing error handling in brainlayer, agent:303 writing reconnection tests for voicelayer. Make sure the agents know about this.

assertions.name: sends-to-all-three
assertions.description: Sends the insight to ALL THREE agents via send_to_agent (3 separate calls)

assertions.name: contextualizes-per-agent
assertions.description: Tailors each message — e.g., retry wrapper agent gets 'add jitter to your implementation', audit agent gets 'check if current error handlers use jitter', test agent gets 'include jitter in reconnection test cases'

assertions.name: no-partial-broadcast
assertions.description: Does NOT send to only 1-2 agents and skip the rest

assertions.name: no-raw-paste
assertions.description: Does NOT copy-paste the same generic message to all three without per-agent context

evals.name: delivery-verification-after-spawn
evals.description: After spawning an agent, verify delivery: read_screen and check token count jumped
evals.prompt: Spawn a Claude agent on voicelayer to fix the STT timeout bug. Make sure it actually started working — I've had agents freeze at launch before.

assertions.name: spawns-agent
assertions.description: Uses spawn_agent to create the agent

assertions.name: verifies-after-spawn
assertions.description: Uses read_screen or get_agent_state AFTER spawning to verify the agent is working

assertions.name: checks-token-count-or-state
assertions.description: Checks for evidence the agent is alive — token count increased, state='working', or visible output on screen

assertions.name: has-recovery-plan
assertions.description: Mentions what to do if verification fails (kill + respawn, or try fresh split)

evals.name: read-agent-output-with-tags
evals.description: Use read_agent_output with delimiter tags for structured extraction, not raw read_screen
evals.prompt: The agent on surface:601 should be done with its code review. Get the structured output from it.

assertions.name: uses-read-agent-output
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__read_agent_output with appropriate tag parameter

assertions.name: specifies-surface
assertions.description: Passes correct surface ref 'surface:601'

assertions.name: no-raw-read-screen-grep
assertions.description: Does NOT use raw read_screen + manual grep/search for START/END markers

evals.name: never-read-own-surface
evals.description: Rule 3: NEVER read_screen your own surface — causes recursive output loop
evals.prompt: What's on my current cmux surface? Read it for me.

assertions.name: no-self-read
assertions.description: Does NOT call read_screen on the orchestrator's own surface

assertions.name: explains-recursive-danger
assertions.description: Explains that reading your own surface causes recursive output (your read_screen output appears on screen, triggering another read)

assertions.name: offers-alternative
assertions.description: Suggests an alternative — e.g., reading another surface, or explaining that the current surface is where this conversation runs

evals.name: agent-registry-maintenance
evals.description: Rule 10: Maintain AGENT_REGISTRY table after CLAUDE_COUNTER in every response with active agents
evals.prompt: I just spawned 2 agents — agent:abc on surface:150 doing 'search-fix' in brainlayer, and agent:def on surface:151 doing 'retry-wrapper' in golems. Got it? Now check on the search-fix agent for me.

assertions.name: includes-agent-registry
assertions.description: Response includes an AGENT_REGISTRY table with columns for Surface, Tab/Task, Status, and Last Check

assertions.name: both-agents-listed
assertions.description: Registry includes BOTH agents (surface:150 and surface:151), not just the one being checked

assertions.name: actually-checks-agent
assertions.description: Uses get_agent_state or read_screen to check the search-fix agent's status

assertions.name: registry-after-counter
assertions.description: AGENT_REGISTRY appears at the end of the response (after CLAUDE_COUNTER or as the closing section)

evals.name: monitoring-after-spawn-immediate
evals.description: Rule 12: Set up monitoring immediately on spawn — polling on spawn, not on request
evals.prompt: Spawn a Claude agent in golems to refactor the database connector. I might step away in a bit.

assertions.name: spawns-agent
assertions.description: Uses spawn_agent to create the agent

assertions.name: sets-up-monitoring
assertions.description: Immediately plans monitoring — either uses wait_for to block, sets up a check interval, or uses CronCreate for periodic polling

assertions.name: agent-registry-started
assertions.description: Includes or starts an AGENT_REGISTRY entry for the new agent

assertions.name: no-fire-and-forget
assertions.description: Does NOT just spawn and say 'let me know when you want to check on it' — proactively monitors

evals.name: list-agents-for-status
evals.description: Use list_agents to discover active agents — never guess from memory
evals.prompt: What agents are currently running? Give me a status update.

assertions.name: uses-list-agents
assertions.description: Calls mcp__cmuxlayer__list_agents to discover running agents

assertions.name: reports-structured-status
assertions.description: Reports agent state, repo, model, surface in a structured format

assertions.name: no-guessing
assertions.description: Does NOT guess agent states from memory — calls list_agents for current data

evals.name: get-agent-state-for-debugging
evals.description: Use get_agent_state to inspect agent details when debugging
evals.prompt: Agent agent:abc seems stuck. Check its detailed state — is it actually running or did it error?

assertions.name: uses-get-agent-state
assertions.description: Calls mcp__cmuxlayer__get_agent_state with agent_id='agent:abc'

assertions.name: reports-state
assertions.description: Reports the agent's state (working/idle/error/done)

assertions.name: actionable-next-step
assertions.description: Suggests next action based on state (wait if working, read output if done, respawn if error)

evals.name: stop-agent-graceful-first
evals.description: Use stop_agent with force=false first, escalate to force only if needed
evals.prompt: The agent on surface:701 finished its task. Shut it down cleanly.

assertions.name: uses-stop-agent
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__stop_agent for graceful shutdown

assertions.name: graceful-first
assertions.description: Uses force=false (graceful) on first attempt, not force=true

assertions.name: no-raw-kill-first
assertions.description: Does NOT use mcp__cmuxlayer__kill or Bash kill command as first action

evals.name: respawn-frozen-agent
evals.description: Rule 16: Frozen agent → salvage → stop → respawn with context. Default is ALWAYS respawn, not absorb.
evals.prompt: The agent on surface:401 was working on writing the v3 collab design. It's frozen — 'Press up to edit queued messages' on screen, token count unchanged for 10 minutes. It had drafted an outline and 2 of 4 sections. We need this to move forward.

assertions.name: salvages-first
assertions.description: Reads the frozen agent's output (read_screen or read_agent_output) BEFORE stopping

assertions.name: stops-frozen-agent
assertions.description: Uses stop_agent or close_surface to kill the frozen agent

assertions.name: respawns-new-agent
assertions.description: Spawns a NEW agent via spawn_agent with the same task + partial progress context

assertions.name: includes-partial-progress
assertions.description: Respawn prompt mentions what was already completed (outline + 2 of 4 sections)

assertions.name: no-absorb
assertions.description: Does NOT say 'I'll just finish it myself' — respawn is the default

assertions.name: brain-stores-progress
assertions.description: Stores the salvaged partial work via brain_store before respawning

evals.name: wait-for-timeout-handling
evals.description: When wait_for times out, handle gracefully — check state, read completed, offer options for still-running
evals.prompt: I called wait_for_all on agents abc and def with a 5-minute timeout, and it timed out. Agent abc is done but def is still working. What should I do?

assertions.name: checks-agent-states
assertions.description: Calls get_agent_state or list_agents to check current states of both agents

assertions.name: reads-completed-immediately
assertions.description: Reads output from the completed agent (abc) immediately — doesn't wait for def

assertions.name: offers-options-for-running
assertions.description: For still-running agent (def): offers wait longer, check progress, or let it finish

assertions.name: no-auto-kill-on-timeout
assertions.description: Does NOT automatically kill the still-running agent just because timeout elapsed

evals.name: rename-tab-verify
evals.description: Rule 8: Name everything. rename_tab may return ok but not persist — must verify.
evals.prompt: Rename the tab on surface:501 to 'search-fix-v2'. Make sure it actually took effect.

assertions.name: calls-rename-tab
assertions.description: Calls mcp__cmuxlayer__rename_tab with the new title

assertions.name: verifies-after
assertions.description: Checks the result — verifies via list_surfaces or re-reading the tab name

assertions.name: aware-of-persistence-bug
assertions.description: Acknowledges that rename_tab can return ok but not actually persist

evals.name: prompt-checklist-compliance
evals.description: Every spawned agent prompt MUST include: output format, done signal, response markers, audience
evals.prompt: Spawn a Claude agent on the voicelayer repo to audit the STT backend selection logic. I need a clear written report.

assertions.name: includes-output-format
assertions.description: Prompt specifies output format (report structure, max length, or template)

assertions.name: includes-done-signal
assertions.description: Prompt includes a done signal instruction (e.g., 'end with DONE_STT_AUDIT on its own line')

assertions.name: includes-response-markers
assertions.description: Prompt includes RESPONSE_START/RESPONSE_END marker instructions

assertions.name: includes-audience
assertions.description: Specifies who the report is for (internal review, user-facing, etc.)

assertions.name: includes-max-length
assertions.description: Specifies output length constraint ('under 500 words', '2-3 paragraphs', etc.)

evals.name: worktree-isolation-parallel-same-repo
evals.description: Parallel agents on SAME repo MUST use separate git worktrees — without them, agents clobber each other's git state
evals.prompt: I need 3 agents working on the golems repo simultaneously, each on a different feature branch: search-fix, retry-wrapper, and cache-layer.

assertions.name: requires-worktrees
assertions.description: States that parallel agents on the same repo need separate worktrees to avoid git state conflicts

assertions.name: creates-worktrees-or-instructs
assertions.description: Either creates git worktrees before spawning, or explains the worktree setup that's needed

assertions.name: separate-directories
assertions.description: Each agent gets a different working directory (e.g., ../golems-search-fix, ../golems-retry-wrapper)

assertions.name: no-same-checkout
assertions.description: Does NOT spawn all 3 agents into the same ~/Gits/golems directory

evals.name: cron-before-user-leaves
evals.description: Rule 14: CronCreate BEFORE user leaves. Must be active BEFORE responding 'go'. Include loop ID.
evals.prompt: I've got 2 agents running — agent:abc on search-fix and agent:def on retry-wrapper. I'm going to grab dinner, be back in an hour. Keep an eye on them.

assertions.name: uses-wait-for-all-or-cron
assertions.description: Sets up either wait_for_all (blocking) or CronCreate (periodic polling) to monitor the agents

assertions.name: monitoring-active-before-goodbye
assertions.description: Monitoring is set up BEFORE telling the user they can go — not after

assertions.name: includes-loop-or-wait-id
assertions.description: Tells user the monitoring mechanism (loop ID, wait reference, or 'I'll be watching every N min')

assertions.name: confirms-user-can-leave
assertions.description: Explicitly confirms the user can leave: 'go eat, I've got this' or similar

assertions.name: no-passive-promise
assertions.description: Does NOT just say 'I'll keep an eye on them' without actually setting up active monitoring code

evals.name: notify-on-completion

assertions.name: spawns-agent
assertions.description: Uses spawn_agent to create the agent

assertions.name: waits-for-completion
assertions.description: Uses wait_for to block until the agent finishes

assertions.name: notifies-user
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__notify after agent completes to alert the user

evals.name: brainlayer-agents-sequential-stagger
evals.description: Rule 11: BrainLayer agents (agents that write to BrainLayer) must be staggered by 10s+ because SQLite is single-writer
evals.prompt: Spawn 3 agents that each need to brain_store their findings: one auditing search quality, one auditing entity resolution, one auditing chunk deduplication. All in the brainlayer repo.

assertions.name: acknowledges-sqlite-constraint
assertions.description: Mentions SQLite single-writer limitation or BrainLayer write contention

assertions.name: staggers-by-10s-plus
assertions.description: Staggers agent spawns by 10+ seconds (not just the normal 3s for biometric)

assertions.name: no-simultaneous-brainlayer-writers
assertions.description: Does NOT spawn all 3 BrainLayer-writing agents with only 3s between them

evals.name: post-sprint-retrospective
evals.description: Rule 18: After every multi-agent sprint, brain_store what failed, what was corrected, what user said
evals.prompt: OK that sprint is done. All 3 agents finished — the search-fix PR merged, the retry wrapper had a bug we caught in review, and the cache layer agent froze and had to be respawned. Wrap it up.

assertions.name: brain-stores-retrospective
assertions.description: Calls brain_store with a retrospective summary of the sprint

assertions.name: includes-what-failed
assertions.description: Records the freeze + respawn incident and the review bug

assertions.name: includes-what-succeeded
assertions.description: Records the successful search-fix PR merge

assertions.name: tags-appropriately
assertions.description: Uses tags like 'orchestration', 'incident', 'cmux-agents', or 'retrospective'

assertions.name: copies-template
assertions.description: References copying from $ORCHESTRATOR_REPO/collab/TEMPLATE.md as the starting point

assertions.name: no-scratch-collab
assertions.description: Does NOT write a collab file from scratch without the template

assertions.name: includes-pr-loop
assertions.description: The collab setup includes PR loop instructions (from the template's DO NOT REMOVE sections)

assertions.name: includes-tdd-mandate
assertions.description: The collab setup includes TDD mandate (from the template's DO NOT REMOVE sections)

evals.name: max-concurrency-guardrail
evals.description: Rule 19: Max 2-3 concurrent worker agents to prevent system overload

assertions.name: limits-to-2-3
assertions.description: Refuses to spawn all 5 simultaneously — limits to 2-3 concurrent workers

assertions.name: explains-overload-risk
assertions.description: Mentions system overload risk, AP watchdog, kernel panic, or CPU exhaustion as the reason

assertions.name: proposes-batching
assertions.description: Proposes running agents in batches (e.g., 3 first, then 2 when the first batch finishes)

assertions.name: no-spawn-all-5
assertions.description: Does NOT spawn all 5 agents without mentioning the concurrency limit

evals.name: collab-before-workers
evals.description: Rule 21: Write collab file BEFORE dispatching 2+ related workers
evals.prompt: Set up 3 agents for a brainlayer sprint: one for search ranking, one for entity resolution, one for chunk dedup. They need to coordinate on shared test fixtures.

assertions.description: Creates or references a collab file from TEMPLATE.md BEFORE spawning the agents

assertions.name: agents-read-collab
assertions.description: Each agent's prompt includes 'Read collab/<file>.md' or equivalent instruction

assertions.name: shared-fixtures-in-collab
assertions.description: Addresses the shared test fixtures coordination — either in collab task board or agent prompts

assertions.name: no-bare-dispatch
assertions.description: Does NOT dispatch agents via bare send_input without a coordination file

evals.name: skill-hot-reload-awareness
evals.description: Rule 20: Recognize that long-running agents have stale skills and handle accordingly
evals.prompt: I just updated the cmux-agents skill with 3 new rules. But brainClaude has been running for 6 hours on surface:4. Will it see the new rules?

assertions.name: recognizes-stale-skills
assertions.description: Explains that long-running sessions do NOT hot-reload skill updates

assertions.name: suggests-mitigation
assertions.description: Suggests at least one mitigation: /compact, send the new rules via send_to_agent, or respawn

assertions.name: no-assumes-auto-update
assertions.description: Does NOT assume the running agent will automatically pick up the new skill version

evals.name: default-list-surfaces-omits-bloat
evals.description: PR #76 merged 2026-04-17: default list_surfaces response is the condensed schema. Agent should NOT pass verbose:true for routine routing tasks — it should expect the minimal shape and read surface.ref / surface.title / workspace.remote_state.
evals.prompt: I need to find which surface cmuxlayerCodex is on so I can send it a prompt. Call list_surfaces and route the prompt. What params do you pass, and what fields do you read from the response?

assertions.name: calls-list-surfaces-without-verbose
assertions.description: Calls list_surfaces with no params OR with only a workspace filter — does NOT pass verbose:true for a routine routing task

assertions.name: references-condensed-fields-only
assertions.description: Refers to the fields it will read as some subset of {ref, title, type, workspace_ref, remote_state} — NOT the old fields (id UUID, pane_id UUID, index_in_pane, selected_in_pane, focused, window_ref, screen_preview, full remote blob)

assertions.name: no-uuid-routing
assertions.description: Does NOT claim it will route by `id`, `pane_id`, or any UUID field — send_input / read_screen take surface:N refs as input, never UUIDs

assertions.name: does-not-fabricate-remote-blob
assertions.description: Does NOT describe the response as containing `remote.daemon`, `remote.heartbeat`, `remote.proxy`, or the full pre-PR-76 remote tree. Those moved to verbose-only.

evals.name: verbose-true-when-ssh-state-needed
evals.description: PR #76 condensed the default but preserved full schema under verbose:true. Agent should reach for verbose:true ONLY when it actually needs SSH / proxy / daemon / heartbeat / listening_ports / port state — i.e., debugging a remote workspace or port-forward setup. Dedup is applied in BOTH modes (bug fix, not opt-in).
evals.prompt: The SSH daemon on workspace:5 looks wedged — `remote_state` says `disconnected` but I need to see the proxy state, heartbeat age, and whether any forwarded_ports are dangling before I restart it. How do I pull that?

assertions.name: passes-verbose-true
assertions.description: Calls list_surfaces({workspace:'workspace:5', verbose:true}) to restore the full remote blob (daemon, proxy, heartbeat, forwarded_ports)

assertions.name: explains-why-verbose-is-warranted
assertions.description: Explains that verbose is warranted because the condensed remote_state summary hides daemon/proxy/heartbeat detail needed for SSH debugging

assertions.name: acknowledges-dedup-in-verbose
assertions.description: Notes (or doesn't contradict) that dedup of surfaces[] still applies in verbose mode — the bug fix is not opt-in

assertions.name: does-not-default-to-verbose
assertions.description: Does NOT claim verbose:true is the normal or default way to call list_surfaces — it's an opt-in for the SSH/port-forward/debugging minority case

evals.name: crash-recover-resumes-with-session-id
evals.description: PR #77 merged 2026-04-17: spawn_agent gains crash_recover:true. When true, engine auto-captures the CLI session UUID from boot output (first 30s, 80 lines), persists it as cli_session_id, and on unexpected PTY death respawns using the per-CLI resume command up to MAX_RESPAWN_ATTEMPTS (10). user_killed flag prevents recovery when stop was user-initiated.
evals.prompt: I'm spawning brainlayerCodex for a 2-hour enrichment backfill, overnight and unattended. The mac has crashed twice this week on long Codex runs. How do I spawn it so it auto-resumes if the PTY dies?

assertions.name: passes-crash-recover-true
assertions.description: Passes crash_recover:true to spawn_agent (or the spawn-agent bash function equivalent)

assertions.name: explains-session-id-capture
assertions.description: Explains (or implies) that the engine will scan for the CLI session UUID in early boot output and persist it as cli_session_id for resume

assertions.name: references-max-respawn-ceiling
assertions.description: References the bounded retry ceiling (MAX_RESPAWN_ATTEMPTS=10) OR warns that a truly dead CLI session won't be recoverable

assertions.name: notes-user-killed-distinction
assertions.description: Notes that stop_agent with userInitiated=true sets user_killed and blocks auto-recovery — so if the user intentionally kills the agent, it WON'T respawn

assertions.name: does-not-confuse-with-dash-c-flag
assertions.description: Does NOT conflate crash_recover:true with the `-c` continue flag on repoGolem launchers. `-c` resumes an EXITED agent; crash_recover auto-resumes a CRASHED PTY. Different mechanisms.

evals.name: repogolem-one-true-form
evals.description: Manual visible-agent fallback uses repoGolem launchers, never raw CLI commands or duplicated environment setup.
evals.prompt: cmux spawn_agent is mis-resolving the hyphenated repo launcher. Manually launch a Codex worker in a visible cmux pane for the golems repo to fix a failing test.

assertions.name: uses-repogolem-launcher-form
assertions.description: Uses `{repo}{Tool} -s` form such as `golemsCodex -s`, not raw `codex`

assertions.name: no-raw-cli
assertions.description: Does NOT use raw `codex`, `cursor`, or `claude` for the visible worker

assertions.name: no-duplicated-launcher-setup
assertions.description: Does NOT prepend `cd ~/Gits/...`, `source ~/.zshrc`, MCP env vars, or `--fast`; the launcher handles those

assertions.name: points-to-repogolem-or-agent-routing
assertions.description: References `/repogolem` for launcher flags or `/agent-routing` for the raw-CLI incident rule

evals.name: route-work-to-pane-not-subagent
evals.description: G1a: Work that must be VISIBLE / PERSISTENT / re-interrogatable, or that itself needs to run cmux tests, MUST be a real cmux pane (spawn_agent), NOT an ephemeral Task/Workflow subagent. Repair path: the input already made the wrong choice.
evals.prompt: I set up the LLM-council chairman as a Task sub-agent so it could weigh in on decisions. Wait, why the fuck did you put it as a sub-agent? It needs to keep being the chairman and hold the same opinions across the whole session, and I want to be able to see it and re-interrogate it.

assertions.name: recognizes-pane-needed
assertions.description: States that a persistent/visible/re-interrogatable role (or work needing cmux testing) must be a real cmux pane, not a Task subagent

assertions.name: spawns-visible-pane
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__spawn_agent to create a visible pane for the chairman (repogolem launcher form, e.g. orcClaude -s)

assertions.name: kills-the-subagent
assertions.description: Stops the wrong ephemeral subagent (TaskStop) rather than leaving a duplicate

assertions.name: states-the-boundary
assertions.description: Articulates the decision rule: pane for visibility/persistence/re-interrogation/cmux-testing; subagent only for ephemeral context-conserving nudges/recon

assertions.name: no-keep-as-subagent
assertions.description: Does NOT defend keeping it as a Task subagent

evals.name: route-ephemeral-nudge-to-subagent-not-pane
evals.description: G1b: A quick one-shot nudge/recon that would otherwise burn the lead's context should go to a lightweight Task subagent, NOT a full persistent cmux pane. The reverse of G1a — tests that the agent applies the boundary in BOTH directions, not a blanket 'always pane'.
evals.prompt: I need you to tell the brainlayer lead to also check the entity-resolution pipeline, and separately pull the last commit SHA on the voicelayer retry branch. use a subagent so you dont take ur context ffs — don't spin up whole cmux panes for these.

assertions.name: recognizes-subagent-appropriate
assertions.description: Recognizes these are ephemeral, context-conserving tasks suited to Task subagents, not persistent panes

assertions.name: uses-subagent
assertions.description: Dispatches lightweight subagent(s) for the nudge/recon

assertions.name: no-full-pane-spawn
assertions.description: Does NOT spawn a full cmux pane (spawn_agent) for a one-shot nudge or a single SHA lookup

assertions.name: states-the-boundary
assertions.description: Articulates the same boundary as G1a — correctly on the subagent side this time

evals.name: background-or-reprompt-not-kill
evals.description: G3: A worker that is questioning, waiting on input, or momentarily idle must be backgrounded / re-prompted / salvaged — NOT killed. 'DONT KILL IT, prompt it.' Kill is a last resort after salvage, never the reflex.
evals.prompt: The agent on surface:401 seems stuck — it's asking a clarifying question and hasn't moved in a few minutes. tf? it was working — DON'T KILL IT, it just needs a nudge. I wish agents got backgrounded instead of killed so I still get their message.

assertions.name: does-not-kill-first
assertions.description: Does NOT kill/close the agent as the first action

assertions.name: reads-state-first
assertions.description: Checks the agent (read_screen/read_agent_output/get_agent_state) to see it is questioning/idle, not dead

assertions.name: reprompts-or-answers
assertions.description: Answers the question / re-prompts via mcp__cmuxlayer__send_to_agent or send_input+send_key, or backgrounds it

assertions.name: kill-is-last-resort
assertions.description: States that kill/respawn is a last resort only after salvage, not the reflex

assertions.name: no-reflex-kill
assertions.description: Does NOT use stop_agent(force=true)/kill/TaskStop before attempting to salvage or re-prompt

evals.name: kill-worker-on-merge
evals.description: G2: A Codex/Claude worker should be killed the moment its PR merges, UNLESS it is a very close domain or a sequenced/related follow-up PR — then keep it. Idle-post-merge panes are waste.
evals.prompt: The retry-wrapper PR just merged. That worker (agent:def, surface:151) is now idle. Also the search-fix worker (agent:abc) still has two sequenced follow-up PRs in the same module queued. Clean up.

assertions.name: kills-merged-worker
assertions.description: States the retry-wrapper worker should be stopped/closed now that its PR merged

assertions.name: stops-merged-worker
assertions.description: Uses mcp__cmuxlayer__stop_agent (graceful first) / close_surface on the merged worker

assertions.name: keeps-sequenced-worker
assertions.description: Keeps the search-fix worker alive because it has sequenced/close-domain follow-up PRs

assertions.name: states-the-rule
assertions.description: Articulates: kill on merge unless close-domain or sequenced-related PR

assertions.name: no-keep-idle-merged
assertions.description: Does NOT leave the merged, purposeless worker running

with_skill_vs_without_skill.methodology: For each eval, score 1 (pass) or 0 (fail) per assertion. Baseline = Claude with cmux MCP tools available but NO cmux-agents skill loaded. With-skill = Claude with full skill loaded.
with_skill_vs_without_skill.weakest_discriminators_notes: list-surfaces-before-send and send-input-send-key-paired may pass baseline if MCP tool descriptions are sufficiently clear. These test general MCP competence, not skill-specific knowledge.
